_meta.status: v0 — FROZEN for the build. Ticket B-T08 validates it; B-T24 calibrates thresholds; B-T26 reports per-code statistics.
why_frozen: The stage-4 model may ONLY emit codes from this list. Out-of-vocabulary codes are dropped by the gate and recorded as rejections with reason 'condition_code_out_of_vocabulary'.
A frozen vocabulary is what makes the output measurable. Free-text condition names cannot be aggregated, cannot be confused-matrixed, and cannot be calibrated against.
It is also what makes the tool honest: a code either has a rule and a measurement path, or it does not exist. There is no room for a confident-sounding condition nobody can grade.
Changing this file after B-T08 requires a DECISIONS.md entry, a version bump, and a re-run of the eval. Do not edit it casually.
integrity_warnings: IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 are TRADEMARKED standards owned by IPC / IPC-WHMA. Their text and official accept/reject photographs are paid material.

These code NAMES are generic industry workmanship terms in widespread public use. They are OUR identifiers. Do NOT present them as IPC clause names, and NEVER invent a clause number. The VERIFY step greps the whole repo for IPC-style clause patterns and fails the build on any hit.

The public statement, verbatim, must appear in README + artifact footer + video + Devpost copy: 'An independent tool aligned to publicly documented electronics workmanship criteria. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified against IPC-A-610 or J-STD-001. Thresholds are ours, calibrated on our own labelled test set.'

Every code with detectable_by='measured' must name measurement_quantities that stage 3 (pure OpenCV) can actually produce. If stage 3 cannot compute it, the code must be 'visual_only' and the model must set measurement_basis='visual_only'. A 'measured' claim without a non-null supporting measurement is downgraded in code.

min_examples_target is for the test set (B-T04). Any code with fewer than 5 real examples at eval time is flagged INSUFFICIENT and gets NO published accuracy number. Publishing 100% on n=2 destroys credibility for everything else.

detectable_by_legend.measured: Stage 3 (pure OpenCV) produces a number that decides it. Strongest evidence class.
detectable_by_legend.visual_only: No reliable metric exists at our resolution; a model may only assert it with an explicit confidence, and it must set measurement_basis='visual_only'. Below the confidence floor it becomes UNDETERMINED, never a verdict.
detectable_by_legend.both: A metric exists but is often not computable (occlusion, missing contour); either path is acceptable and the basis must be declared.

class_sensitivity_legend.class_sensitive: The verdict can differ between Class 1, 2 and 3. This is what makes the class slider meaningful.
class_sensitivity_legend.class_independent: A reject at every class. Knowing WHICH criteria are class-independent is itself domain knowledge and is worth saying on camera.

deliberately_excluded.reason: Indistinguishable from INSUFFICIENT_SOLDER_VOLUME at our image resolution and without a reference view of the same board. Merged into INSUFFICIENT_SOLDER_VOLUME with value=0 as the extreme case.
Overlaps WIRE_STRAND_DAMAGE and COMPONENT_DAMAGE. Splitting it would create a code humans cannot label consistently, which would depress kappa for no gain.
Out of scope: this is a JOINT-level tool, not a board-level cosmetic inspector. Stated in LIMITATIONS.md.
Out of scope for the same reason; also not measurable from a single macro photo.

deliberately_excluded.candidate: ANY code requiring cross-section, X-ray or ICT
deliberately_excluded.reason: Not obtainable from the input we accept. VOIDING_EXCESSIVE is retained only because it is assessable optically for non-BGA joints; for BGA it MUST abstain with reason 'modality_mismatch_bga_optical'.

codes.title: No defect detected
codes.plain_english: Nothing on our rule table fired for this joint. Note what this means: it is NOT a guarantee of quality, it is the absence of a detected condition.
observable_signs: concave fillet with visible flow onto pad and lead
smooth bright surface
no bridging, spikes, blobs or debris
component seated flat
correct polarity marking orientation
codes.disambiguation_hint: Absence of a fired rule, not a positive identification of goodness. If the image is uncalibrated or blurry this code MUST NOT be emitted — the correct output is UNDETERMINED. A clean-looking unmeasurable joint is the single most dangerous false positive available to this tool.
codes.reporting_note: Reported separately from ACCEPT in the eval, because 'no rule fired' and 'a rule evaluated and passed' are different claims.

codes.title: Insufficient wetting
codes.plain_english: The solder did not spread onto the metal. It sits as a bead and pulls away from the pad, often with a dull surface. The joint may look present but it is not bonded.
observable_signs: solder beads up rather than flowing
visible gap or a steep angle at the pad edge
dull or grainy surface
the pad edge is visible under the solder
codes.disambiguation_hint: The distinguishing feature is the ANGLE at the pad edge, not the amount of solder. A joint can have plenty of solder and still not wet. If wetting_angle_deg is not computable (no clear pad-edge contour), declare measurement_basis='visual_only' — do not estimate the angle.
codes.measurement_caveat: wetting_angle_deg requires a resolvable pad-edge contour and a perpendicular-ish view. From an oblique phone photo it is frequently not computable. That is expected; abstain rather than guess.

codes.title: Insufficient solder volume
codes.plain_english: Not enough solder. The fillet is thin or missing over part of the joint, so the mechanical and electrical connection is weak.
observable_signs: thin or concave-to-hollow fillet
part of the lead or pad has no solder on it
the joint outline is visible as a skeleton
codes.disambiguation_hint: Volume is about QUANTITY, wetting is about SPREAD. Label both if both are present — they are separate codes and a joint can carry two. This is why findings are a list per ROI, not a single label.
codes.measurement_caveat: solder_volume_ratio needs a reference for what 'enough' means for this joint geometry. Without calibration (mm_per_px) the ratio is scale-free and still usable; fillet_area_mm2 is NOT and requires calibrated=true.

codes.title: Excess solder
codes.plain_english: Too much solder. You should still be able to see the shape of the joint underneath; a shiny ball that hides the lead is over-application.
observable_signs: convex rather than concave fillet
the joint outline is obscured
solder extends beyond the pad
a rounded blob
codes.disambiguation_hint: Excess only becomes a bridge if it touches another conductor, and only becomes an icicle if it forms a spike. Check for those first (higher priority rules) before labelling plain excess.
codes.reporting_note: Often a PROCESS_INDICATOR rather than a reject at Class 1–2. Emitting the middle grade here is what stops the tool reading as naive to production people.

codes.title: Solder bridge
codes.plain_english: Solder connects two electrically separate conductors. This is a short circuit.
observable_signs: a continuous solder path between two pads or pins
two joint blobs merged
solder spanning a gap that should be open
codes.disambiguation_hint: A bridge is a CONDUCTIVE path; webbing is a thin non-structural filament. If you cannot tell, treat it as a bridge — a false positive on a short is far cheaper than a false negative.
codes.reporting_note: Class-independent: a short is a short at every reliability class. The Class-3 minimum clearance is a margin, not a change in kind. Say this on camera — it shows the difference between class-sensitive and class-independent criteria is understood.

codes.title: Icicle
codes.plain_english: A sharp spike of solder projecting from the joint. It can break off and become debris, or short against something nearby.
observable_signs: a tapering spike of solder
solder projecting from the joint at an angle
a stalactite shape below a hand-soldered joint
codes.disambiguation_hint: The distinguishing feature is aspect ratio: an icicle is long and thin. Measure length and width from the mask and compute the ratio; below a threshold it is excess, above it is an icicle.
codes.measurement_caveat: Most common on hand-soldered through-hole joints, which are also the joints most likely to be photographed obliquely. Expect a high not-computable rate and abstain honestly.

codes.title: Solder ball / splash
codes.plain_english: Loose detached blobs of solder left on the board. They can move later and cause a short.
observable_signs: small discrete bright spheres on the board surface
not connected to any joint
often near a hand-soldered joint or a reworked area
codes.disambiguation_hint: A ball is DETACHED and roughly spherical. Solder still attached to the joint is excess or an icicle, not a ball. Clearance to the nearest exposed conductor is what makes it dangerous, so measure that too.
codes.measurement_caveat: Very small balls are near the resolution limit of a phone macro shot. Below min_roi_px they are not detectable and the code must not be emitted — report the detection floor in LIMITATIONS.md.

codes.title: Solder webbing / filament
codes.plain_english: A thin filament of solder stretching between two points. It may or may not be conductive, and it is fragile.
observable_signs: a hair-thin solder strand
spanning between pins or pads
often after hot-air rework
codes.disambiguation_hint: A loose wire strand is copper-coloured and usually traceable to a termination; webbing is solder-coloured and usually traceable to a joint. Colour and origin both matter. If genuinely ambiguous, label SOLDER_BRIDGE — the conservative call.
codes.measurement_caveat: Thin filaments are easily lost to thresholding. Expect a high not-computable rate; a visual_only path with an explicit confidence is legitimate here.

codes.title: Tombstoning
codes.plain_english: One end of a two-terminal chip component has stood up like a tombstone. That end is not soldered at all.
observable_signs: the component body is visibly raised at one end
a shadow under the lifted end
one termination has no solder contact
codes.disambiguation_hint: Tombstoning is a rotation about the transverse axis with ONE end lifted clear; skiing is a smaller tilt with both ends still down. If the lift is ambiguous, prefer SKIING_TILTED_COMPONENT — it is the less severe claim.
codes.measurement_caveat: tombstone_lift_deg REQUIRES the component body contour to be visible against the board. When it is not, stage 3 MUST return value=null with reason 'component_contour_not_resolvable' and the gate MUST abstain. Never estimate an angle from a single 2D view without the body contour — that is exactly the 'hallucination with a decimal point' failure this project exists to avoid.

codes.title: Skiing / tilted component
codes.plain_english: The component sits at an angle rather than flat, but both ends are still down. A milder condition than tombstoning.
observable_signs: a visible gap or shadow under one side
the body is not parallel to the board
solder fillets asymmetric
codes.disambiguation_hint: Both ends down = skiing; one end clear = tombstoning. In-plane rotation or offset = misalignment. Three different conditions that a single 'component is crooked' label would collapse.
codes.measurement_caveat: Highly sensitive to camera angle. A perspective-corrected or near-perpendicular shot is required; otherwise abstain.

codes.title: Head-in-pillow
codes.plain_english: The lead or ball sits in a bed of solder without having bonded to it. It looks soldered from above. Detecting it from a single optical view is usually impossible.
observable_signs: a visible seam between the lead and the solder mass
no concave fillet at the interface
the solder surface looks undisturbed under the component
codes.disambiguation_hint: For BGA this is essentially undetectable optically. If the joint type is bga, the model should NOT assert this code; the honest output is UNDETERMINED with reason 'measurement_not_computable'. Including the code at all is a statement that we know it exists and that we know we cannot see it — which is more credible than pretending.
codes.reporting_note: Expected to be flagged INSUFFICIENT at eval time (n<5). That is the correct outcome; publish no accuracy for it and explain why in LIMITATIONS.md.

codes.title: Misaligned component
codes.plain_english: The component is offset or rotated in-plane relative to its pads, so one side overhangs or one fillet is missing.
observable_signs: the body overhangs a pad
fillets asymmetric left to right
the component is rotated relative to the pad outline
a lead sits between pads
codes.disambiguation_hint: Misalignment is IN-PLANE (offset/rotation about the board normal); skiing and tombstoning are OUT-OF-PLANE. From a single perpendicular photo you can see the first and barely the second — which is why the calibration and view-angle checks matter.
codes.measurement_caveat: Requires the pad outline to be visible. On a solder-masked board with pads fully covered, offset is not computable and the code must not be asserted.

codes.title: Disturbed joint
codes.plain_english: The joint moved while the solder was solidifying, so it has a grainy, frosted surface instead of being smooth. It looks soldered but it is weak.
observable_signs: frosted or granular surface texture
irregular crystalline appearance
dull rather than bright
surface cracks or folding lines
codes.disambiguation_hint: Surface TEXTURE is the signal, not shape or quantity. This is a texture problem, and texture is exactly what a single macro photo carries well — which is why it is a legitimate visual_only code rather than a cop-out.
codes.reporting_note: Class-independent by construction: a disturbed joint is not acceptable at any class. One of the codes worth naming on camera when explaining that not every criterion is class-sensitive.

codes.title: Cold joint
codes.plain_english: The solder did not reach proper temperature, so it is dull, grainy and poorly bonded. Overlaps heavily with a disturbed joint.
observable_signs: dull matte surface
poor flow and a lumpy outline
the solder looks like it sat on the surface rather than alloyed with it
codes.disambiguation_hint: Honest note: DISTURBED_JOINT and COLD_JOINT are frequently indistinguishable from a single photograph, and humans disagree about them too. That is expected and it is DATA — record the disagreement notes (B-T30) and publish the kappa for this pair specifically. A tool that admits where humans also disagree is more trustworthy than one that pretends to resolve it.
codes.reporting_note: Expect the lowest inter-rater agreement in the whole vocabulary. Publishing that number is a deliberate credibility move, not a weakness.

codes.title: Solder crack
codes.plain_english: A visible crack through the solder mass, usually from fatigue, thermal cycling or movement during solidification.
observable_signs: a dark line through the solder
a crack following the lead outline
a separation between the solder and the lead or pad
codes.disambiguation_hint: A crack is a LINEAR dark feature within the solder mass. A shadow from oblique lighting can look exactly like one — check the light direction and, where available, a second view. False positives from shadows are the main risk here.
codes.reporting_note: Likely INSUFFICIENT at eval time. Publish no accuracy for it; explain that cracks in a 4-day test set of hand-made boards are rare.

codes.title: Excessive voiding
codes.plain_english: Air bubbles trapped inside the solder. Too many weaken the joint and trap heat.
observable_signs: dark rounded regions inside the solder mass
surface pits where a void broke through
an irregular internal texture
codes.disambiguation_hint: ⚠ MODALITY RULE: for joint_type='bga', voiding is normally assessed by X-RAY, not optically. An optical void_fraction for a BGA is almost certainly invalid — the gate MUST abstain with reason 'modality_mismatch_bga_optical' unless the user supplies an X-ray image, in which case ImageContext.modality='xray' and the assessment is legitimate. Knowing this is itself an insider signal.
codes.measurement_caveat: Only surface-breaking and near-surface voids are visible optically. Report void_fraction as an OPTICAL estimate with the method stated, never as a true volume fraction.

codes.title: Pin hole / blow hole
codes.plain_english: A small hole in the solder surface, usually from trapped gas or flux vapour escaping during solidification.
observable_signs: a small round crater in the solder surface
often at the top of a through-hole fillet
a dark circular depression
codes.disambiguation_hint: A pin hole is a SURFACE-BREAKING void; excessive voiding is internal. From one photo you mostly see the surface-breaking ones, which is worth stating rather than hiding.
codes.reporting_note: Expected INSUFFICIENT (n<5). Fine — flag it and move on.

codes.title: Excessive flux residue
codes.plain_english: Leftover flux gunk. Some is normal; a lot traps moisture and can be corrosive or conductive.
observable_signs: a translucent or amber film around the joint
a white crystalline residue
residue bridging two conductors
a discoloured halo on the solder mask
codes.disambiguation_hint: Flux residue is a FILM with soft edges, contamination is usually discrete and irregular. Detecting it is colour-space dependent and highly sensitive to white balance, and no-clean flux behaves differently from rosin. Record the flux type when known; when unknown, widen the abstention band and say so.
codes.measurement_caveat: The single most lighting-sensitive code in the vocabulary. Any eval number for it must be reported together with the lighting conditions of the test set, or it is meaningless.

codes.title: Insulation clearance violation
codes.plain_english: Solder or a stray wire strand is too close to the board surface or to the next conductor. It can arc or short.
observable_signs: solder nearly touching the board surface
a strand reaching toward an adjacent pad
less clearance than the surrounding joints
codes.disambiguation_hint: This is the code for 'not touching, but too close'. It is a clearance judgement and therefore REQUIRES calibration — without mm_per_px the concept of 'too close' has no meaning. If calibrated=false, this code MUST NOT be emitted and the answer is UNDETERMINED with reason 'uncalibrated'.
codes.measurement_caveat: The clearest example in the whole vocabulary of why the calibration check exists. Use it in the video when explaining insight #2.

codes.title: Wire strand damage / splayed strands
codes.plain_english: Some of the small copper wires inside the cable are cut, bent back, folded under, or sticking out. The joint is weaker than it looks.
observable_signs: strands splaying outside the termination
strands folded under the solder
a reduced strand count visible at the entry
strands protruding beyond the solder
codes.disambiguation_hint: Counting SEVERED strands from a single photo is usually not possible — you can see splaying and protrusion, not how many are missing inside. Prefer the visual_only path with an explicit confidence and abstain below the floor. Do not invent a strand count.
codes.measurement_caveat: Exposure length is measurable; strand count generally is not. Stage 3 must return value=null with reason 'insufficient_resolution' for any count-based quantity.

codes.title: Component damage
codes.plain_english: The part itself is cracked, chipped, burnt or its terminations are damaged. Nothing about the solder can save it.
observable_signs: a crack or chip in the component body
a missing corner
discolouration or scorching
a damaged, lifted or missing termination
deformation of a connector housing
codes.disambiguation_hint: Damage to the COMPONENT vs damage to the BOARD (lifted land) vs a placement problem (misalignment). Three different repair actions and three different owners — which is why they are three codes.

codes.title: Lifted land / pad
codes.plain_english: The copper pad has peeled up off the board. The joint is hanging on by nothing.
observable_signs: the pad is visibly raised or curled
a gap between the pad and the substrate
the pad has moved with the component
exposed substrate where the pad should be
codes.disambiguation_hint: Tombstoning lifts the COMPONENT and leaves the pad down; a lifted land takes the PAD with it. Look at the pad edge, not the body. This distinction decides whether the repair is a re-placement or a board repair — a materially different outcome for the technician.
codes.reporting_note: Likely INSUFFICIENT (n<5) unless you deliberately manufacture them by overheating pads. Doing so is cheap and makes the test set much stronger — see data/testset-protocol.md §2.

codes.title: Polarity marking mismatch
codes.plain_english: The part is fitted backwards. Diodes, electrolytic capacitors, ICs and connectors all have a direction.
observable_signs: the component marking faces the opposite way to the board marking
a cathode band on the wrong side
a pin-1 dot misaligned with the pad-1 indicator
a keyed connector inserted the wrong way round
codes.disambiguation_hint: ⚠ PRECONDITION: this code applies ONLY when BOTH a component polarity marking AND a board polarity marking are visible. If either is not visible, ABSTAIN — do not guess. A 180°-rotation misalignment without visible markings is not a polarity finding, it is at most MISALIGNED_COMPONENT.
codes.reporting_note: The precondition is the important part and it is worth calling out in the video: a tool that refuses to judge polarity when it cannot see both markings is a tool that understands what it is looking at.

codes.title: Contamination / foreign material
codes.plain_english: Something that should not be there is on or near the joint: debris, a cut lead, tape residue, metal swarf, or a foreign particle.
observable_signs: a discrete particle not part of the joint
a cut lead offcut resting on the board
tape or adhesive residue
metal swarf or drill debris
fibres or dust embedded in flux
codes.disambiguation_hint: A solder ball IS solder and is usually near a joint; foreign material is not solder and may be anywhere. Conductive debris is the dangerous case, and conductivity is not visible — which is why clearance matters more than identification here.
codes.reporting_note: A catch-all by nature. Keep its confidence floor high so it does not become a place to dump uncertain findings — a catch-all that absorbs uncertainty silently is how a tool starts looking confident about nothing.

acceptance_checks.vocabulary_validation: python scripts/validate_vocabulary.py --strict → exactly 24 codes, unique, every code has plain_english, observable_signs (≥3), detectable_by, class_sensitivity, min_examples_target, confusable_with and a disambiguation_hint
acceptance_checks.rule_coverage: every code maps to ≥1 rule in data/rules/workmanship-rules.json, and every rule maps to ≥1 code (bidirectional check)
acceptance_checks.measurement_coverage: every code with detectable_by='measured' names ≥1 quantity that stage 3 can actually produce; the set of quantities used is a subset of the Measurement.quantity enum in schemas/core-schemas.json
acceptance_checks.no_invented_clause_numbers: grep the entire repo for IPC-style clause patterns (e.g. 'IPC-A-610 [0-9]', 'J-STD-001 [0-9]', '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+') and FAIL THE BUILD on any hit. This is a hard legal and credibility line.
acceptance_checks.model_constraint: the stage-4 prompt embeds this list verbatim; a test feeds a deliberately out-of-vocabulary response and asserts the gate drops it with reason 'condition_code_out_of_vocabulary'
acceptance_checks.disclaimer_present: the required public statement appears verbatim in README.md, the PDF artifact footer, the video end card and the Devpost description

eval_reporting_rules: Report a per-code confusion matrix and precision/recall/F1 for every code with n ≥ 5.
Flag every code with n < 5 as INSUFFICIENT and publish NO accuracy number for it. Say why in LIMITATIONS.md.
Report Cohen's kappa for the whole vocabulary AND separately for the pairs flagged as confusable — especially DISTURBED_JOINT vs COLD_JOINT, where low agreement is expected and is itself a finding.
Report the count of out-of-vocabulary model emissions and the count of 'measured' claims downgraded to 'visual_only'. Both are trust metrics, not errors to hide.

Expected INSUFFICIENT codes at n=120–300: HEAD_IN_PILLOW, PIN_HOLE_BLOW_HOLE, SOLDER_CRACK, LIFTED_LAND. Plan for that in the test set (deliberately manufacture them) or accept it and publish it honestly.
